Quick mutual action plan (high level):

- Week 2: Dry-run smoke tests against staging endpoints — Grace + Integrio
- Week 3: Production cutover weekend (target: 2028-04-02) + post-cutover monitoring

Attached: integrio_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (single-sheet MAP with owners/dates). Also see a short SDK snippet below you can start with (Python, requests + backoff):

# sample-snippet-start
import requests
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry

session = requests.Session()
retries = Retry(total=5, backoff_factor=0.5, status_forcelist=[429, 502, 503, 504])
session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))

# Default timeout: connect 2s, read 10s
response = session.post(
    'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate',
    headers={'Authorization': 'Bearer <REDACTED>', 'X-Request-ID': 'integrio-1234'},
    json={'model': 'redwood-large', 'input': '...'},
    timeout=(2, 10)
)
# Check X-RateLimit-* headers for dynamic throttling decisions
# sample-snippet-end

Implementation notes (summary):
- We recommend client-side exponential backoff on 429 with jitter; prefer Retry-After header when present.
- Set a conservative per-request timeout (connect + read) and move long-running work to async job workers.
- Use our streaming endpoints for low-latency interactive flows.

Next steps: can we schedule a 45-min technical handoff on Monday to walk the team through the SDK snippet and the staging endpoints? I can get Karthik and a runtime engineer on the call.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor

Hi Sam / Grace — attaching a short technical checklist and a tiny patch with examples for SDK instrumentation (also attaching sdk-instrumentation-sample.patch). Main points below.

Endpoint migration notes:
1) Staging (no SLA): https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate — use for dry-run only.
2) Production (new): https://api.redwood.ai/v1/v2/generate — this is a backwards-compatible v2 path; we maintain the v1 path for 60 days after cutover.

Curl example (safe cutover):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/v2/generate" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}'

Go snippet for instrumentation (net/http + context):
// sample-go-start
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 12*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req, _ := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/v2/generate", bytes.NewBuffer(payload))
req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+key)
req.Header.Set("X-Client-Name", "integrio-service")
// read X-RateLimit-* headers on response and adapt local limiter
// sample-go-end

Retries/limits guidance (technical):
- Respect X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset. Use a local token-bucket limiter for smoothing bursts.
- For batched workloads, batch size impacts latency and cost — prefer smaller batches with concurrency for tail latency sensitive paths.
- If you rely on prefix caching: include a deterministic cache key (model+prefix_hash+params) and set a short TTL (minutes) to avoid staleness during rollout.

Instrumentation: include X-Request-ID on every request and ship request/response latencies to your observability backend. We can provide a small client middleware if you want (attached patch).

- Rate-limit pattern: combine server-side token bucket with client-side smoothing. If you see 429s, backoff with full-jitter and prefer Retry-After when provided.
